claims.title: Rise of the Srivijaya thalassocracy
claims.summary: From its base at Palembang in Sumatra, the Buddhist kingdom of Srivijaya comes to dominate maritime trade through the Straits of Malacca and Sunda and becomes a renowned centre of Buddhist scholarship.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Indonesia: From the spice islands and the temples of Java to Southeast Asia's largest democracy.", terralore.co/country/IDN/chronicle#ev-671-rise-of-the-srivijaya-thalassocracy, claim TL:IDN:event:671:rise-of-the-srivijaya-thalassocracy, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Construction of Borobudur
claims.summary: Under the Sailendra dynasty in central Java the great Buddhist monument of Borobudur is built; the world's largest Buddhist temple, it is today a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Indonesia: From the spice islands and the temples of Java to Southeast Asia's largest democracy.", terralore.co/country/IDN/chronicle#ev-780-construction-of-borobudur, claim TL:IDN:event:780:construction-of-borobudur, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding of the Majapahit empire
claims.summary: Raden Wijaya establishes Majapahit in eastern Java, which grows into the most powerful Hindu-Buddhist empire of the archipelago.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Indonesia: From the spice islands and the temples of Java to Southeast Asia's largest democracy.", terralore.co/country/IDN/chronicle#ev-1293-founding-of-the-majapahit-empire, claim TL:IDN:event:1293:founding-of-the-majapahit-empire, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Majapahit's golden age under Hayam Wuruk
claims.summary: Under King Hayam Wuruk and his prime minister Gajah Mada, Majapahit reaches its height, projecting power and trade across much of the archipelago.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Indonesia: From the spice islands and the temples of Java to Southeast Asia's largest democracy.", terralore.co/country/IDN/chronicle#ev-1350-majapahit-s-golden-age-under-hayam-wuruk, claim TL:IDN:event:1350:majapahit-s-golden-age-under-hayam-wuruk, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Islam takes root in northern Sumatra
claims.summary: The early Muslim sultanate of Samudera Pasai in northern Sumatra marks the establishment of Islam in the archipelago, spread by traders along the maritime routes.

sources.label: History of Indonesia (Islamic influence; Dutch rule)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Indonesia: From the spice islands and the temples of Java to Southeast Asia's largest democracy.", terralore.co/country/IDN/chronicle#ev-1297-islam-takes-root-in-northern-sumatra, claim TL:IDN:event:1297:islam-takes-root-in-northern-sumatra, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Rise of the Demak Sultanate on Java
claims.summary: Demak emerges as the first major Islamic state on Java and a base from which Islam spreads across the island as Majapahit's power collapses.

sources.label: History of Indonesia (Islamic influence; Dutch rule)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Indonesia: From the spice islands and the temples of Java to Southeast Asia's largest democracy.", terralore.co/country/IDN/chronicle#ev-1475-rise-of-the-demak-sultanate-on-java, claim TL:IDN:event:1475:rise-of-the-demak-sultanate-on-java, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Spice sultanates of Ternate, Tidore and Aceh flourish
claims.summary: Muslim sultanates controlling the clove, nutmeg and pepper trade grow rich and powerful, making the archipelago the hub of a global spice economy.

sources.label: History of Indonesia (Islamic influence; Dutch rule)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Indonesia: From the spice islands and the temples of Java to Southeast Asia's largest democracy.", terralore.co/country/IDN/chronicle#ev-1500-spice-sultanates-of-ternate-tidore-and-aceh, claim TL:IDN:event:1500:spice-sultanates-of-ternate-tidore-and-aceh, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Portuguese capture of Malacca
claims.summary: Afonso de Albuquerque seizes the trading city of Malacca, beginning sustained European involvement in the archipelago's spice trade.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Indonesia: From the spice islands and the temples of Java to Southeast Asia's largest democracy.", terralore.co/country/IDN/chronicle#ev-1511-portuguese-capture-of-malacca, claim TL:IDN:event:1511:portuguese-capture-of-malacca, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding of the Dutch East India Company (VOC)
claims.summary: The Dutch Republic charters the VOC with sweeping powers to trade, wage war and govern, launching nearly two centuries of company rule in the Indies.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Indonesia: From the spice islands and the temples of Java to Southeast Asia's largest democracy.", terralore.co/country/IDN/chronicle#ev-1602-founding-of-the-dutch-east-india-company-voc, claim TL:IDN:event:1602:founding-of-the-dutch-east-india-company-voc, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding of Batavia
claims.summary: Governor-General Jan Pieterszoon Coen storms Jayakarta and builds Batavia (modern Jakarta) as the VOC's Asian headquarters.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Indonesia: From the spice islands and the temples of Java to Southeast Asia's largest democracy.", terralore.co/country/IDN/chronicle#ev-1619-founding-of-batavia, claim TL:IDN:event:1619:founding-of-batavia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Banda massacre
claims.summary: To enforce the nutmeg monopoly, Coen's forces kill, starve, enslave or deport almost the entire population of the Banda Islands, an atrocity that destroys Bandanese society.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Indonesia: From the spice islands and the temples of Java to Southeast Asia's largest democracy.", terralore.co/country/IDN/chronicle#ev-1621-the-banda-massacre, claim TL:IDN:event:1621:the-banda-massacre, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Dissolution of the VOC
claims.summary: Bankrupt after decades of war, debt and corruption, the VOC is dissolved and its possessions pass to the Dutch state, ushering in direct colonial rule.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Indonesia: From the spice islands and the temples of Java to Southeast Asia's largest democracy.", terralore.co/country/IDN/chronicle#ev-1799-dissolution-of-the-voc, claim TL:IDN:event:1799:dissolution-of-the-voc, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Cultivation System
claims.summary: The Dutch impose the Cultuurstelsel, forcing Javanese peasants to grow export crops for the colonial state; it enriches the Netherlands while causing widespread hardship and local famines.

sources.label: History of Indonesia (Islamic influence; Dutch rule)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Indonesia: From the spice islands and the temples of Java to Southeast Asia's largest democracy.", terralore.co/country/IDN/chronicle#ev-1830-the-cultivation-system, claim TL:IDN:event:1830:the-cultivation-system, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding of Budi Utomo
claims.summary: The cultural society Budi Utomo is founded, widely regarded as the start of organised Indonesian nationalism and the National Awakening.

sources.label: Indonesia (toward independence; Japanese occupation; after Suharto)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Indonesia: From the spice islands and the temples of Java to Southeast Asia's largest democracy.", terralore.co/country/IDN/chronicle#ev-1908-founding-of-budi-utomo, claim TL:IDN:event:1908:founding-of-budi-utomo, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Sukarno founds the Indonesian National Party
claims.summary: Sukarno establishes the PNI, demanding full independence and giving the nationalist movement a charismatic mass leader.

sources.label: Indonesia (toward independence; Japanese occupation; after Suharto)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Indonesia: From the spice islands and the temples of Java to Southeast Asia's largest democracy.", terralore.co/country/IDN/chronicle#ev-1927-sukarno-founds-the-indonesian-national-party, claim TL:IDN:event:1927:sukarno-founds-the-indonesian-national-party, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Youth Pledge (Sumpah Pemuda)
claims.summary: Young nationalists vow to recognise one Indonesian motherland, nation and language, a foundational moment in forging a unified national identity.

sources.label: Indonesia (toward independence; Japanese occupation; after Suharto)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Indonesia: From the spice islands and the temples of Java to Southeast Asia's largest democracy.", terralore.co/country/IDN/chronicle#ev-1928-the-youth-pledge-sumpah-pemuda, claim TL:IDN:event:1928:the-youth-pledge-sumpah-pemuda, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Japanese occupation of the Indies
claims.summary: Japan conquers the Dutch East Indies, ending Dutch rule; its occupation brings forced labour and hardship but also mobilises and arms Indonesian nationalists.

sources.label: Indonesia (toward independence; Japanese occupation; after Suharto)
Japanese occupation of the Dutch East Indies

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Indonesia: From the spice islands and the temples of Java to Southeast Asia's largest democracy.", terralore.co/country/IDN/chronicle#ev-1942-japanese-occupation-of-the-indies, claim TL:IDN:event:1942:japanese-occupation-of-the-indies, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Proclamation of Independence
claims.summary: Sukarno and Mohammad Hatta proclaim Indonesia an independent republic in Jakarta, days after Japan's surrender; they become president and vice-president the next day.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Indonesia: From the spice islands and the temples of Java to Southeast Asia's largest democracy.", terralore.co/country/IDN/chronicle#ev-1945-proclamation-of-independence, claim TL:IDN:event:1945:proclamation-of-independence, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Indonesian National Revolution
claims.summary: Indonesians wage a four-year armed and diplomatic struggle against Dutch attempts to reimpose colonial rule, enduring two major Dutch offensives and heavy losses.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Indonesia: From the spice islands and the temples of Java to Southeast Asia's largest democracy.", terralore.co/country/IDN/chronicle#ev-1945-the-indonesian-national-revolution, claim TL:IDN:event:1945:the-indonesian-national-revolution, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Recognition of sovereignty
claims.summary: Following the Round Table Conference in The Hague, the Netherlands formally transfers sovereignty and recognises the independence of Indonesia.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Indonesia: From the spice islands and the temples of Java to Southeast Asia's largest democracy.", terralore.co/country/IDN/chronicle#ev-1949-recognition-of-sovereignty, claim TL:IDN:event:1949:recognition-of-sovereignty, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The anti-communist mass killings
claims.summary: Following the 30 September coup attempt blamed on the PKI, an army-led purge kills an estimated 500,000 to over a million suspected communists and others, a vast atrocity that paves Suharto's path to power.

sources.label: Indonesia: US Documents Released on 1965-66 Massacres

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Indonesia: From the spice islands and the temples of Java to Southeast Asia's largest democracy.", terralore.co/country/IDN/chronicle#ev-1965-the-anti-communist-mass-killings, claim TL:IDN:event:1965:the-anti-communist-mass-killings, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Suharto's New Order
claims.summary: Suharto formally becomes president and rules for over three decades, delivering growth and stability through authoritarian control, military dominance and pervasive corruption.

sources.label: Indonesia (toward independence; Japanese occupation; after Suharto)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Indonesia: From the spice islands and the temples of Java to Southeast Asia's largest democracy.", terralore.co/country/IDN/chronicle#ev-1968-suharto-s-new-order, claim TL:IDN:event:1968:suharto-s-new-order, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Fall of Suharto and Reformasi
claims.summary: Amid economic collapse and mass protests, Suharto resigns after 32 years in power, launching the Reformasi era of democratic reform and decentralisation.

sources.label: Indonesia (toward independence; Japanese occupation; after Suharto)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Indonesia: From the spice islands and the temples of Java to Southeast Asia's largest democracy.", terralore.co/country/IDN/chronicle#ev-1998-fall-of-suharto-and-reformasi, claim TL:IDN:event:1998:fall-of-suharto-and-reformasi, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: First direct presidential election
claims.summary: Indonesians directly elect their president for the first time, consolidating one of the world's largest democracies after the authoritarian New Order.

sources.label: Indonesia (toward independence; Japanese occupation; after Suharto)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Indonesia: From the spice islands and the temples of Java to Southeast Asia's largest democracy.", terralore.co/country/IDN/chronicle#ev-2004-first-direct-presidential-election, claim TL:IDN:event:2004:first-direct-presidential-election, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
